summary: A desktop app with a React interface and Rust logic connected through generated TypeScript bindings.
description: Give Rust application logic a React desktop interface through generated TypeScript bindings. A thin Tauri shell exposes typed commands and live channels, while a transport facade lets the same interface run against browser fixtures. Tests cover Rust logic, bindings and the mocked interface. The starting app shows application information and a live tick; filesystem workflows, persistence and other desktop behavior are features you implement.
seoDescription: A Tauri desktop app recipe with React, Rust library crates, generated IPC types and a mock transport for browser development and tests.

projectExamples.title: Local file inspection tool
projectExamples.description: Implement Rust file parsing behind typed commands and display the results in React. Add explicit filesystem permissions and handling for large or invalid files.

projectExamples.title: Desktop process monitor
projectExamples.description: Replace the demonstration tick channel with application measurements and charts. Platform integrations, permissions and data retention remain product work.

requests: build desktop windows that call my Rust code with checked types
preview my desktop interface in a browser using sample data
show live updates from Rust in my app window
goodFor: sharing types between Rust and TypeScript
testing interfaces through a mock transport
caveats: Browser previews and Playwright use a mock transport; the packaged webview needs a manual check.
App bundles target the developer's OS; Linux shell builds require WebKitGTK system packages.
